docs.title: ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph
docs.text:
Where Knowledge Connects, Agents Reason.

An enterprise-ready Hybrid Document Intelligence Platform built with Google Agent Development Kit (ADK). Authenticate with Neon PostgreSQL, ingest documents through a live 5-step dual vector + graph pipeline, explore interactive Neo4j knowledge topologies, and converse with a multi-tool reasoning agent.

Start building Interactive User Guide System Architecture adk_rag — hybrid_rag_kg_agent ADK Agent Hybrid SQL Neo4j Cypher FastAPI 
from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent
from app.rag_store import hybrid_search, vector_search
from app.graph_store import graph_search, get_entity_relationships

root_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="hybrid_rag_kg_agent",
    model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    instruction=build_agent_instruction,
    tools=[
        hybrid_search,
        vector_search,
        graph_search,
        get_entity_relationships,
    ],
)
-- 70% pgvector HNSW Cosine + 30% PostgreSQL GIN Full-Text
SELECT chunk_id, filename, content,
       (0.7 * (1 - (embedding <=> %(query_vec)s::vector)) +
        0.3 * ts_rank_cd(
          to_tsvector('english', content),
          plainto_tsquery('english', %(query)s)
        )) AS combined_score
FROM document_chunks
WHERE user_id = %(user_id)s
ORDER BY combined_score DESC LIMIT 5;
// Multi-Hop Tenant-Isolated Neo4j Knowledge Graph Traversal
MATCH (s:Entity {user_id: $user_id})
      -[r:RELATES_TO {user_id: $user_id}]->
      (t:Entity {user_id: $user_id})
WHERE toLower(s.name) CONTAINS $term
   OR toLower(r.fact) CONTAINS $term
RETURN s.name AS source, r.relation_type AS relation,
       t.name AS target, r.fact AS fact
LIMIT 15;
@app.post("/chat", response_model=ChatResponse)
async def chat_endpoint(
    req: ChatRequest,
    current_user:  dict = Depends(get_current_user),
):
    result = await ask_agent(
        question=req.question,
        user_id=current_user["user_id"],
        session_id=req.session_id,
    )
    return ChatResponse(**result)

Key architectural and operational answers about ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph:

Why combine Neon pgvector Hybrid Search with a Neo4j Knowledge Graph?

Vector similarity excels at conceptual semantics, and PostgreSQL Full-Text Search (ts_rank_cd) captures exact technical identifiers, acronyms, and SKUs. However, neither represents explicit multi-hop relationships across documents. By extracting structured (:Entity)-[:RELATES_TO]->(:Entity) triplets into Neo4j during ingestion and exposing all four tools to the Google ADK LlmAgent, the agent can combine local passage evidence with global graph topology in a single turn.

How does the 5-step dual ingestion pipeline work in real time?

When a user uploads a file via POST /upload, the backend updates an in-memory per-user stage tracker polled every 800ms by the React UI (GET /ingest/progress): (1) Document parsing (pypdf / python-docx / UTF-8), (2) Paragraph-aware chunking (1200 chars, 200 overlap), (3) Batched 768-dim embeddings via gemini-embedding-001, (4) Neon PostgreSQL document_chunks indexing (HNSW + GIN), and (5) Gemini 2.5 Flash structured entity/relationship extraction into Neo4j.

How is multi-tenant data isolation enforced across Neon and Neo4j?

Every user authenticates against the Neon PostgreSQL users table using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (120,000 iterations) and receives a signed HS256 JWT token. Every SQL query filters on WHERE user_id = %(user_id)s, every Neo4j node ID is namespace-prefixed (user_id::entity_name) with {user_id: $user_id} property filters, and ADK chat sessions are keyed by (app_name, user_id, session_id).

How does the Google ADK LlmAgent decide which retrieval tool to call?

The hybrid_rag_kg_agent is initialized with dynamic runtime instructions via build_agent_instruction(ReadonlyContext) and four function tools: hybrid_search (default for factual/technical queries), vector_search (for broad conceptual similarity), graph_search (for discovering entities and relationship facts), and get_entity_relationships (for 1-hop neighborhood inspection). Gemini 2.5 Pro autonomously invokes one or multiple tools before synthesizing a grounded response.

What happens when a user deletes a document?

Calling DELETE /documents/{document_id} performs an atomic cascade across both databases: it deletes the document and its document_chunks from Neon PostgreSQL, removes all [:RELATES_TO {document_id}] edges and the (:Document) node in Neo4j, and automatically prunes any orphaned (:Entity) nodes that no longer have any remaining relationships or document mentions.

How do I deploy the platform to production?

The backend deploys as a Python web service on Render (or Google Cloud Run) connected to serverless Neon PostgreSQL and Neo4j AuraDB, while the Vite + React frontend deploys to Netlify. Full configuration templates (render.yaml, netlify.toml) and environment variable checklists are provided in the Cloud Deployment Guide.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform is engineered as a modular, multi-tenant Hybrid Document Intelligence system combining Google Agent Development Kit (google-adk), Gemini 2.5, Neon Console Serverless PostgreSQL (pgvector + Full-Text Search), and Neo4j.

docs.title: Architectural Pillars
docs.text:
• Neon PostgreSQL Authentication

    Stateless HS256 JWT Bearer authentication backed by a users table in Neon PostgreSQL with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (260,000 iterations) password hashing.

  • 5-Step Dual Ingestion Engine

    Asynchronous worker pipeline with SHA-256 content-hash deduplication & atomic version replacement that parses 13 document formats, chunks text semantically, embeds in batches (768-dim), indexes in Neon Postgres, and extracts entities into Neo4j.

  • Google ADK Multi-Tool Agent

    LlmAgent (gemini-2.5-pro) equipped with 4 specialized retrieval tools (hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) and dynamic user context injection.

  • Interactive Bioluminescent UI

    React 18 + Vite single-page workspace featuring real-time per-step ingestion telemetry, tool execution badges, dual citations, and an interactive SVG Neo4j topology explorer.

docs.title: 2. Backend Module Architecture (app/)
docs.text: Module File Responsibility Configuration app/config.py Loads .env, validates GOOGLE_API_KEY, configures DATABASE_URL, NEO4J_*, JWT_*, AGENT_MODEL, and GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL. Database Layer app/database.py Manages the Neon PostgreSQL ThreadedConnectionPool (with TCP keepalives, connection health checks, and URL normalization) and the Neo4j driver (GraphDatabase.driver). Automatically initializes pgvector, tables, HNSW/GIN indexes, and Neo4j constraints on startup. Authentication app/auth.py Implements PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (260,000 iterations), HS256 JWT signing/verification, user registration/login against the Neon users table, and the get_current_user FastAPI security dependency. Format Parsers app/parsers.py Dispatches uploaded files by extension (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .log) to specialized text extractors. Semantic Chunker app/chunking.py Splits extracted document text along markdown headers, paragraphs, and sentences (chunk_size=1200, overlap=200) to preserve semantic coherence. Embeddings app/embeddings.py Wraps google-genai gemini-embedding-001 (768 dimensions) with batching (50 chunks per call) for high-throughput document ingestion and single-query embedding. Vector & Hybrid Store app/rag_store.py Executes Neon PostgreSQL CRUD (add_document_chunks, delete_document_chunks, list_user_documents) and retrieval (search_documents pure vector cosine search and hybrid_search_documents combining 70% vector similarity + 30% ts_rank_cd full-text score). Knowledge Graph Store app/graph_store.py Extracts structured ExtractedEntity and ExtractedRelationship objects from chunks using gemini-2.5-flash and persists/queries them in Neo4j via parameterized Cypher queries. Dual Ingestion Pipeline app/ingest.py Orchestrates the 5-step ingestion pipeline and maintains real-time per-user step telemetry (_user_ingestion_progress) polled by the frontend UI. Google ADK Agent app/agent.py Defines root_agent (LlmAgent) equipped with 4 tools (hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) and dynamic system instructions injecting the active user_id. REST API app/api.py Exposes FastAPI endpoints for Auth, Upload, Live Ingestion Progress, Documents, Knowledge Graph, and Agentic Chat. Runs heavy ingestion in asyncio.to_thread using OS temp storage (/tmp/adk_rag_uploads) so Uvicorn --reload is never interrupted.

docs.title: 4. Multi-Tenant Security & Data Isolation
docs.text:
Defense-in-Depth Tenant Partitioning

Every data record across the entire stack is partitioned by the authenticated user_id extracted from the verified HS256 JWT token:

  1. Authentication Layer (app/auth.py): Extracts and verifies the user_id (sub claim) on every protected API request.
  2. Neon PostgreSQL (app/rag_store.py): Every SELECT and DELETE query enforces WHERE user_id = %s.
  3. Neo4j Knowledge Graph (app/graph_store.py): Every node ID is prefixed with <user_id>:: (e.g., user_123::postgresql) and every Cypher MATCH filters on {user_id: $user_id}.
  4. Google ADK Session Context (app/agent.py): ADK chat sessions are keyed by (app_name, user_id, session_id) and build_agent_instruction(ReadonlyContext) injects the active user_id directly into the agent's system prompt.

docs.title: Agentic Chat & Graph Tools
docs.text: The chat subsystem uses Google Agent Development Kit (google-adk) and Gemini (gemini-2.5-pro) to reason across both Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector + Full-Text Search) and the Neo4j Knowledge Graph.

docs.title: Multi-Tool Agent Architecture (app/agent.py)
docs.text:
The root agent (root_agent) is an instance of google.adk.agents.LlmAgent configured with four specialized tools:

flowchart TD
    Question["User Question in Agentic Chat"] --> Agent["Google ADK LlmAgent (gemini-2.5-pro)"]
    Agent -->|Exact terms + semantics| T1["1. hybrid_search (70% pgvector cosine + 30% PostgreSQL FTS)"]
    Agent -->|Broad conceptual similarity| T2["2. vector_search (100% pgvector cosine similarity)"]
    Agent -->|Entities & factual triplets| T3["3. graph_search (Neo4j Entity & RELATES_TO keyword match)"]
    Agent -->|1-hop / 2-hop graph neighborhood| T4["4. get_entity_relationships (Neo4j Cypher neighborhood traversal)"]
    T1 --> Synthesis["Synthesized Markdown Response with Tool Badges + Citations"]
    T2 --> Synthesis
    T3 --> Synthesis
    T4 --> Synthesis

docs.title: 1. hybrid_search(query, user_id, top_k=5)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/rag_store.py -> hybrid_search_documents()
  • How It Works: Embeds query with gemini-embedding-001 (768-dim) and runs a single SQL query on Neon PostgreSQL combining cosine similarity (0.7 weight) and English full-text rank ts_rank_cd (0.3 weight).
  • Best For: Technical questions, specific names, numbers, dates, and general factual questions over uploaded documents.

docs.title: 2. vector_search(query, user_id, top_k=5)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/rag_store.py -> search_documents()
  • How It Works: Queries document_chunks ordered purely by pgvector cosine distance (embedding <=> query_vec).
  • Best For: Conceptual, thematic, or paraphrased queries where exact keywords may not appear in the source text.

docs.title: 3. graph_search(query, tool_context)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/graph_store.py -> search_knowledge_graph()
  • How It Works: Tokenizes the query and searches Neo4j (:Entity) names, dynamically inferred domain categories (entity_type), descriptions, and [:RELATES_TO] facts scoped to user_id.
  • Best For: Discovering how any domain entities, subjects, attributes, items, processes, or categories connect, relate, depend on each other, or compare across one or more documents.

docs.title: 4. get_entity_relationships(entity_name, tool_context)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/graph_store.py -> get_entity_relationships_from_graph()
  • How It Works: Finds the matching (:Entity) node in Neo4j (regardless of category) and traverses all incoming and outgoing [:RELATES_TO] edges.
  • Best For: Deep-diving into a specific named entity's direct neighborhood, dependencies, and supporting facts.

docs.title: Dynamic User Context Injection
docs.text:
To guarantee that the agent always queries only the signed-in user's data without asking the user for their ID, build_agent_instruction(readonly_context: ReadonlyContext) dynamically injects the authenticated user_id into the system prompt on every turn:

def build_agent_instruction(readonly_context: ReadonlyContext) -> str:
    user_id = "default_user"
    if readonly_context and getattr(readonly_context, "session", None):
        user_id = getattr(readonly_context.session, "user_id", None) or "default_user"
    return (
        f"... The current authenticated user's `user_id` is EXACTLY: \"{user_id}\". "
        f"Whenever you call ANY tool, you MUST pass `user_id=\"{user_id}\"` ..."
    )

docs.title: Tool Execution Tracking & Dual Citations
docs.text:
In app/api.py, the /chat endpoint inspects the ADK event stream (event.get_function_calls()) during runner.run_async(...) and collects the ordered list of invoked tool names into tools_used:

{
  "status": "success",
  "question": "How does the platform store vectors and knowledge graph facts?",
  "answer": "The platform stores 768-dimensional embeddings in Neon PostgreSQL [Source: architecture.md, chunk 0] and extracts entities into Neo4j [Graph: FastAPI Backend -> USES -> Neo4j].",
  "tools_used": ["hybrid_search", "graph_search"],
  "session_id": "session_a8b9c0",
  "user_id": "user_9f8e7d6c5b4a3210"
}

The frontend ChatMessage.jsx component renders: - Tool Execution Badges at the top of the assistant message bubble (hybrid_search, graph_search) - Source Chunk Citations: [Source: filename, chunk N] - Knowledge Graph Citations: [Graph: EntityA -> RELATION -> EntityB]

docs.title: Deployment Guide

  2. Copy your pooled connection string (postgresql://user:pass@ep-...pooler...neon.tech/dbname?sslmode=require).

docs.text:
1. Push your repository to GitHub.
  2. Sign in to Render and create a new Web Service connected to your repository.
  3. Configure the service (or use the included render.yaml Blueprint):

  8. GOOGLE_API_KEY: Your Gemini API key

  10. JWT_SECRET_KEY: A strong random secret key for signing JWT tokens
  11. JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS: 168
  12. NEO4J_URI: Your Neo4j AuraDB URI (neo4j+s://...)
  13. NEO4J_USERNAME: neo4j
  14. NEO4J_PASSWORD: Your Neo4j password
  15. NEO4J_DATABASE: neo4j
  16. AGENT_MODEL: gemini-2.5-pro
  17. GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL: gemini-2.5-flash
  18. TOP_K: 5
  19. Deploy and copy your live Render URL (e.g., https://adk-rag-backend.onrender.com).

1. Sign in to Netlify and click Add new site → Import an existing project.
  2. Select your GitHub repository and configure:
  3. Base directory: frontend

  7. VITE_API_URL: Your Render backend URL (without a trailing slash)

docs.title: Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text: The 5-step dual ingestion pipeline converts raw uploaded files into both searchable 768-dimensional vector chunks in Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector) and structured entities and relationships in the Neo4j Knowledge Graph, while streaming real-time step progress to the UI.

docs.title: 5-Step Dual Ingestion Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Upload["Uploaded File (app/api.py -> /tmp/adk_rag_uploads)"] --> Step1["Step 1: Format-Specific Text Extraction (app/parsers.py)"]
    Step1 --> Step2["Step 2: Structure-Aware Semantic Chunking (app/chunking.py — 1200 chars, 200 overlap)"]
    Step2 --> Dedup{"SHA-256 Content-Hash & Filename Check (app/rag_store.py)"}
    Dedup -->|"Same Filename + Same Hash (unchanged)"| FastSkip["Skip Redundant Indexing & Return Existing Metrics"]
    Dedup -->|"Different Filename + Same Hash (duplicate_content)"| FastSkip
    Dedup -->|"Same Filename + Modified Hash (updated)"| PurgeOld["Atomically Purge Previous Chunks (Postgres) & Triples (Neo4j)"]
    PurgeOld --> Step3["Step 3: Batched Gemini Embeddings (app/embeddings.py — gemini-embedding-001, 768-dim)"]
    Dedup -->|"New Document (created)"| Step3
    Step3 --> Step4["Step 4: Neon PostgreSQL Indexing (app/rag_store.py — pgvector HNSW + FTS GIN)"]
    Step4 --> Step5["Step 5: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction (app/graph_store.py — gemini-2.5-flash Structured JSON)"]

docs.title: Redundant & Updated File Upload Handling (v2.1.1)
docs.text:
After Step 2, ingest_document computes a normalized SHA-256 content fingerprint (hashlib.sha256(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.strip()).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()) and calls find_existing_user_document(...) in app/rag_store.py to handle all three redundant/updated upload scenarios automatically:

Scenario Condition ingest_action Pipeline Behavior UI Badge 1. Exact Same File Re-Uploaded same filename + same content_hash "unchanged" Skips redundant Gemini embedding & Neo4j extraction calls, fast-completes Step 5, and returns existing document counts. Skipped (Already Indexed) 2. Same Content, Different Filename different filename + same content_hash "duplicate_content" Prevents duplicate vector chunks and duplicate graph triples from polluting retrieval; references duplicate_of. Skipped (Duplicate of <filename>) 3. Updated Version of Existing File same filename + different content_hash "updated" Atomically deletes the previous version from Neon PostgreSQL (delete_document_chunks) and Neo4j (delete_document_from_graph), then indexes the new version through Steps 3–5. Updated Version 4. Brand-New Document No filename or content hash match "created" Runs the full 5-step dual ingestion pipeline and stores content_hash in documents.metadata. Indexed (New)

docs.title: Step 1: Lossless Docling, Multimodal Vision & Format-Specific Extraction (app/parsers.py)
docs.text:
extract_text(file_path) uses IBM Docling (docling.document_converter.DocumentConverter) combined with Gemini 2.5 Flash Multimodal Vision (v2.3.3) and lossless format-specific extractors so zero text, tables, embedded figures/diagrams, headers, footers, or speaker notes are lost:

  • Eliminating <!-- image --> Content Loss (v2.3.3):
  • Docling is initialized with PdfPipelineOptions(do_ocr=True, do_table_structure=True, generate_picture_images=True, images_scale=2.0) and export_to_markdown(traverse_pictures=True).
  • Every embedded figure, chart, diagram, or screenshot across .pdf, .docx, and .pptx is extracted, filtered to skip tiny decorative icons (< 48px), and transcribed via Gemini 2.5 Flash Vision (_transcribe_image_with_gemini) into structured Markdown text, tables, and component relationships, replacing each <!-- image --> placeholder in-place.
Extension Library Extraction Details .pdf docling (DocumentConverter) + pymupdf (fitz) + Gemini Vision Converts multi-column layouts, headings, tables, and embedded figures/diagrams into structured Markdown via Docling TableFormer + Gemini Vision, reconciled page-by-page with PyMuPDF (page.get_text("text", sort=True) + page.find_tables()). .docx docling + python-docx + Gemini Vision Preserves document order across headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, all Word tables (w:tbl as Markdown tables), section headers/footers, and embedded figures. .xlsx, .xls docling + openpyxl Loads workbook with data_only=True and formats every sheet as a GitHub-Flavored Markdown table under ## [Sheet: Name]. .pptx docling + python-pptx + Gemini Vision Recursively extracts text frames, grouped shapes (shape.shapes), slide tables (shape.has_table as Markdown tables), speaker notes (notes_slide), and embedded slide diagrams/images. .html, .htm docling + HTMLParser Converts HTML headings, lists, and <table> elements into structured Markdown. .csv csv + Markdown formatter Converts CSV rows into a structured Markdown table with column headers. .txt, .md, .json, .xml, .log Built-in open() Reads UTF-8 text directly without truncation.

docs.title: Step 2: Structure & Table-Aware Semantic Chunking (app/chunking.py)
docs.text:
Instead of slicing text at arbitrary character offsets (which breaks sentences and tables mid-thought), chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1200, overlap=200) preserves document structure:

  1. Line Normalization: Converts to and collapses 3+ consecutive newlines into .
  2. Paragraph & Header Segmentation: Splits along paragraph breaks ( ) and Markdown headings (#, ##, ###).
  3. Greedy Paragraph Packing: Accumulates complete paragraphs into the current chunk as long as total length remains \(\le 1200\) characters.
  4. Markdown Table Header Preservation (_split_markdown_table_block): If a Markdown table exceeds 1200 characters, splits cleanly along row boundaries ( ) and repeats the table header row (| Col 1 | Col 2 | | --- | --- |) at the top of each continuation chunk.
  5. Sentence-Boundary Fallback: If a single prose paragraph exceeds 1200 characters, splits along sentence boundaries ((?<=[.!?])\s+).
  6. Contextual Overlap: Carries the trailing 200 characters of chunk \(i\) into the start of chunk \(i+1\) so concepts spanning chunk boundaries remain intact.

docs.title: Step 3: Batched Gemini Embedding Generation (app/embeddings.py)
docs.text:
get_embeddings_batch(texts, batch_size=50) generates 768-dimensional vectors for all chunks using gemini-embedding-001:

response = client.models.embed_content(
    model="gemini-embedding-001",
    contents=batch,
    config=types.EmbedContentConfig(output_dimensionality=768),
)

Batching up to 50 chunks per API request significantly reduces ingestion latency compared to sequential per-chunk calls.

docs.title: Step 4: Neon PostgreSQL Vector + Full-Text Indexing (app/rag_store.py)
docs.text:
add_document_chunks(...) inserts the document metadata into documents and bulk-inserts all chunks into document_chunks using psycopg2.extras.execute_values:

  • Vector Index (pgvector HNSW): Indexes embedding vector_cosine_ops for fast cosine similarity search.
  • Full-Text Index (PostgreSQL GIN): Indexes to_tsvector('english', content) for keyword and phrase matching.

docs.title: Step 5: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction (app/graph_store.py)
docs.text:
add_document_to_graph(...) extracts domain entities and factual relationships from the chunks and merges them into Neo4j:

  1. Structured LLM Extraction:
  2. Sends batches of 4 chunks to gemini-2.5-flash configured with response_mime_type="application/json" and response_schema=ChunkGraphExtraction.
  3. Extracts canonical ExtractedEntity nodes (name, category, description) and ExtractedRelationship edges (source, target, relation_type, fact).
  4. Neo4j Cypher Persistence:
  5. Creates/merges the (:Document {id: user_id::document_id}) node.
  6. Merges each (:Entity {id: user_id::lower(name)}) node and links (e)-[:MENTIONED_IN]->(d).
  7. Merges directed (source:Entity)-[:RELATES_TO {relation_type, document_id, user_id}]->(target:Entity) edges storing the supporting fact.
  8. Metadata Sync:
  9. Updates documents.entities_count and documents.relationships_count in Neon PostgreSQL so the Documents tab displays accurate counts for every file.

docs.title: Live Per-User & Multi-Document Progress Tracking (app/ingest.py)
docs.text:
When a user selects multiple files in UploadTab.jsx, App.jsx orchestrates sequential batch ingestion (doc_index = 1..N, total_docs = N) so each document runs through Steps 1–5 (0% → 100%) cleanly.

During ingestion, ingest_document(file_path, filename, user_id, doc_index, total_docs) updates _ingestion_progress[user_id] before and after each of the 5 stages. The frontend polls GET /ingest/progress every 450ms while an upload is active, receiving:

  "total_docs": 2,
  "current_step": 5,
  "step_name": "Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction",
  "message": "Extracting domain entities & relationships with Gemini into Neo4j…",
  "step_outputs": {
    "1": "Extracted 1,142 characters from ADK_Architecture_Brief.md",
    "2": "Created 2 overlapping semantic chunks",
    "3": "Generated 2 × 768-dim embedding vectors",
    "4": "Indexed 2 chunks in Neon pgvector + FTS"

docs.title: How to Get Each Environment Variable
docs.text: Clicking the ⓘ How to get? icon next to any variable in the Settings tab jumps directly to its corresponding section below.

docs.title: 1. GOOGLE_API_KEY (Google AI Studio)
docs.text:
GOOGLE_API_KEY authenticates the backend with Google's Gemini API for agent reasoning (gemini-2.5-pro), knowledge graph extraction (gemini-2.5-flash), and vector embeddings (gemini-embedding-001).

  1. Open Google AI Studio — Get API Key and sign in with your Google account.
  2. Click Create API key in the top-right corner.
  3. Select an existing Google Cloud project or click Create API key in new project.
  4. Copy the generated key (starts with AIzaSy...) and paste it into GOOGLE_API_KEY in the Settings tab or .env.
  5. Fallback behavior: If left blank in the UI, the platform automatically falls back to the GOOGLE_API_KEY defined in .env.

docs.title: 2. AGENT_MODEL (ADK Reasoning Model)
docs.text:
AGENT_MODEL specifies the Gemini model used by the Google ADK LlmAgent (app/agent.py) to orchestrate tool calls (hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) and synthesize cited answers.

  • Recommended / Default Value: gemini-2.5-pro
  • Supported Alternatives: gemini-2.5-flash (faster, lower latency)
  • Fallback behavior: If left blank, automatically defaults to gemini-2.5-pro.

docs.title: 3. GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL (Neo4j Extractor Model)
docs.text:
GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL specifies the Gemini model used during Step 5 (Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction) to extract structured JSON entities and relationships from document chunks.

  • Recommended / Default Value: gemini-2.5-flash
  • Fallback behavior: If left blank, automatically defaults to gemini-2.5-flash.

docs.title: 4. EMBEDDING_MODEL (Vector Embedding Model)
docs.text:
EMBEDDING_MODEL specifies the Gemini embedding model used in Step 3 and during query time to generate 768-dimensional semantic vectors stored in Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector).

  • Recommended / Default Value: gemini-embedding-001
  • Fallback behavior: If left blank, automatically defaults to gemini-embedding-001 (768 dimensions).

docs.title: 5. DATABASE_URL (Neon Console PostgreSQL)
docs.text:
DATABASE_URL connects the platform to Neon Serverless PostgreSQL for user authentication (users), document metadata (documents), and 768-dim pgvector + Full-Text Search (document_chunks).

  1. Go to Neon Console and sign up or log in (Free Tier includes pgvector).
  2. Click New Project, choose a project name (e.g., adk_rag), select a region close to you, and click Create project.
  3. On your project Dashboard, locate the Connection Details card.
  4. Ensure Connection pooling is enabled and copy the PostgreSQL connection string: 
    postgresql://neondb_owner:YOUR_PASSWORD@ep-xxx-pooler.us-east-1.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require
  5. Paste the full URI into DATABASE_URL in the Settings tab or .env.
  6. Automatic Schema Creation: On connection, app/database.py automatically runs CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; and creates all required tables and HNSW/GIN indexes.
  7. Fallback behavior: If left blank in the UI, falls back to DATABASE_URL in .env.

docs.title: 6. JWT_SECRET_KEY & JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS (Authentication Security)
docs.text:
• JWT_SECRET_KEY: Secret string used with HMAC-SHA256 to sign and verify Bearer session tokens when users sign in.
  • When you run ./setup.sh or setup.bat, a 64-character cryptographic hex secret is generated automatically.
  • You can also generate one manually with: 
    python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"
  • Fallback behavior: If left blank, falls back to the .env secret or a deterministic derived key.
  • JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS: Number of hours a signed login session remains valid.
  • Default Value: 168 (7 days).

docs.title: 7. NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD & NEO4J_DATABASE (Neo4j AuraDB)
docs.text:
These variables connect the platform to Neo4j for storing and traversing your Knowledge Graph ((:Document), (:Entity), [:RELATES_TO]).

  1. Open Neo4j Aura Console and sign in.
  2. Click New Instance → select AuraDB Free → click Create.
  3. Important: A modal will appear displaying your Generated Password. Click Download and continue (which saves a .txt credentials file) or copy the password immediately:
  4. NEO4J_URI: Copy the Connection URI from your AuraDB instance card (e.g., neo4j+s://xxxxxxxx.databases.neo4j.io). For a local Docker/Desktop Neo4j instance, use bolt://localhost:7687.
  5. NEO4J_USERNAME: Default is neo4j.
  6. NEO4J_PASSWORD: Paste the generated AuraDB password.
  7. NEO4J_DATABASE: Default is neo4j.
  8. Wait until your AuraDB instance status turns Running, then click Save & Apply Connections in the Settings tab.
  9. Fallback behavior: Any field left blank automatically falls back to its default value (NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j, NEO4J_DATABASE=neo4j, and .env credentials).

docs.title: 8. TOP_K (Hybrid Retrieval Depth)
docs.text:
TOP_K controls how many top-scoring document chunks are returned per call to hybrid_search and vector_search.

  • Recommended / Default Value: 5 (valid range: 1 to 50).
  • Fallback behavior: If left blank, automatically defaults to 5.

docs.title: 9. LangSmith Observability & Evaluation
docs.text:
Configure optional LangSmith tracing and experiment syncing (v2.4.0). Even without a LangSmith API key, the Evaluation tab still runs locally using Gemini 2.5 Flash as the LLM-as-a-Judge.

  • LANGSMITH_TRACING: Set to true to stream live Google ADK agent chains (/chat) and retrieval tool spans (vector_search, hybrid_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) to LangSmith. Defaults to false.
  • LANGSMITH_API_KEY: Personal or workspace API key (lsv2_pt_...) generated at smith.langchain.com → Settings → API Keys.
  • LANGSMITH_PROJECT: Target LangSmith project name for traces and evaluation experiments. Defaults to adk-agentic-rag.
  • LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT: LangSmith API endpoint (https://api.smith.langchain.com for US, or https://eu.api.smith.langchain.com for EU).

docs.title: Step 4: Start the FastAPI Server
docs.text:
uvicorn app.api:app --reload

Verify the server is running: - API Root / Health: http://localhost:8000/health - Interactive Swagger Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: 3. Frontend Setup
docs.text:
Open a second terminal window:

cd /path/to/adk_rag/frontend
npm install
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:5173 in your browser to access the application.

docs.title: 4. Building & Serving the MkDocs Documentation
docs.text:
To view this documentation site in your browser with the Material theme and Mermaid diagrams:

source .venv/bin/activate
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001

Open http://127.0.0.1:8001 in your browser.

• Normalized SHA-256 Content Fingerprinting: Every uploaded document's extracted text is normalized (re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.strip())) and hashed with SHA-256, stored in documents.metadata.content_hash in Neon PostgreSQL (with automatic backfill for pre-v2.1.1 rows).
  • Three-Scenario Redundant & Updated File Handling (find_existing_user_document):
  • Exact Same File Uploaded Again (same filename + same content_hash → ingest_action: "unchanged"): Skips redundant Gemini embedding and Neo4j LLM extraction calls, fast-completes Step 5, and returns the existing document metrics (Skipped (Already Indexed)).
  • Same Content with Different Filename (different filename + same content_hash → ingest_action: "duplicate_content"): Prevents duplicate vector chunks and duplicate graph triples from polluting retrieval rankings and returns the existing document reference (Skipped (Duplicate of <existing_filename>)).
  • Updated Version of an Existing File (same filename + different content_hash → ingest_action: "updated"): Atomically purges the previous version's chunks from Neon PostgreSQL (delete_document_chunks) and its relationships/orphaned entities from Neo4j (delete_document_from_graph) before indexing the updated document (Updated Version).
  • Brand-New Document (no match → ingest_action: "created"): Executes the full 5-step dual ingestion pipeline (Indexed (New)).

  • 768-Dim pgvector HNSW + Full-Text Search (tsvector): Replaced legacy ChromaDB/Pinecone storage with a unified Neon PostgreSQL schema (users, documents, document_chunks) indexed with HNSW Cosine (vector_cosine_ops) and GIN Full-Text Search (to_tsvector).
  • Weighted Hybrid Retrieval Formula: Combines 70% dense semantic vector similarity (1 - (embedding <=> query_vec)) with 30% lexical keyword ranking (ts_rank_cd) in a single SQL query.

  • Idempotent Cypher Upserts & Atomic Cascade Deletion: Merges (:Document)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Entity) and (:Entity)-[:RELATES_TO]->(:Entity) triples into Neo4j and atomically cleans up both Neon PostgreSQL and Neo4j (including orphan entity pruning) when a document is deleted (DELETE /documents/{doc_id}).

docs.title: 2. Database Schemas & Indexing
3. Authentication & Cryptographic Security (app/auth.py)
docs.text:
• Password Hashing (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256)

    • Work Factor: 260,000 iterations (OWASP standard)
    • Salt: 16 cryptographic random bytes (32 hex chars) per user via secrets.token_hex(16)
    • Verification: Constant-time digest comparison via hmac.compare_digest()

  • Stateless Bearer Token (HS256 JWT)

    • Algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 signed with JWT_SECRET_KEY
    • Default TTL: 168 hours (7 days, configurable via JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS)
    • Claims: sub (user_id), email, name, iat, exp

docs.title: 4.1 Structure-Aware Semantic Chunker (app/chunking.py)
docs.text:
• Chunk Size: 1,200 characters
  • Sliding Overlap: 200 characters
  • Splitting Priority: Markdown headings (#, ##, ###) → double-newline paragraphs (\n\n) → sentence boundaries ((?<=[.!?])\s+) → hard character slice fallback.

docs.title: 4.2 Batched Vector Embeddings (app/embeddings.py)
docs.text:
• Model: gemini-embedding-001
  • Output Dimensionality: 768 floats
  • Batch Size: Up to 50 chunks per API request

docs.title: 4.3 Hybrid Search Scoring Formula (app/rag_store.py)
docs.text:
For a user query \(q\) with embedding \(\mathbf{e}_q \in \mathbb{R}^{768}\) and a candidate chunk \(c\) with embedding \(\mathbf{e}_c \in \mathbb{R}^{768}\):

  1. Cosine Vector Similarity (pgvector <=> cosine distance operator): $\(\text{vector\_similarity}(c, q) = 1 - \left( \mathbf{e}_c \iff \mathbf{e}_q \right)\)$

  2. Full-Text Cover-Density Rank (PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd): $\(\text{keyword\_score}(c, q) = \text{ts\_rank\_cd}\left(\text{to\_tsvector}(\text{'english'}, c.\text{content}),\ \text{plainto\_tsquery}(\text{'english'}, q)\right)\)$

  3. Weighted Hybrid Score (70% semantic + 30% lexical): $\(\text{combined\_score}(c, q) = 0.7 \times \text{vector\_similarity}(c, q) + 0.3 \times \text{keyword\_score}(c, q)\)$

docs.title: 5. Gemini Structured Output Schema (app/graph_store.py)
docs.text:
During Step 5 of ingestion, chunks are grouped in batches of 4 (up to 25 chunks per document) and passed to gemini-2.5-flash with response_mime_type="application/json" and temperature=0.1:

class ExtractedEntity(BaseModel):

    category: str      # Person | Organization | Technology | Concept | Location | Event | Process | Metric | Model

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: Solutions for common issues encountered when running the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform.

docs.title: ERROR: database "...sslmode=require" does not exist or connection is insecure (try using sslmode=require)
docs.text:
Cause: The DATABASE_URL in .env was missing the ? query separator before sslmode=require.

Fix: Ensure your DATABASE_URL in .env includes ?sslmode=require: 

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@ep-xxx.region.aws.neon.tech/dbname?sslmode=require
(Note: app/database.py also includes _normalize_database_url() to auto-repair missing ? delimiters at runtime.)

docs.title: Neo4j GqlStatusObject 01N51: warn: relationship type does not exist (RELATES_TO)
docs.text:
Cause: Neo4j 5+ emits informational GQL notifications when querying relationship types or node labels on a newly created, empty database before any document has been ingested.

Fix: 1. app/database.py suppresses these harmless notifications via NotificationMinimumSeverity.OFF. 2. Restart uvicorn app.api:app --reload or upload your first document to create the initial :Entity and :RELATES_TO elements.

docs.title: Neo4j connection warning on startup
docs.text:
Cause: NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD, or NEO4J_DATABASE in .env does not match your running Neo4j instance, or your Neo4j AuraDB instance is paused.

Fix: - Check your credentials in .env. - If using Neo4j AuraDB Free tier, verify in the Aura Console that your instance is Running (Aura Free instances pause after inactivity) and that NEO4J_DATABASE matches your database name.

docs.title: [vite] http proxy error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8000
docs.text:
Cause: The Vite frontend dev server (http://localhost:5173) is trying to proxy API requests to http://127.0.0.1:8000, but the FastAPI backend is not running.

Fix: Start the FastAPI backend in a terminal from the project root: 

source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn app.api:app --reload

docs.title: [vite] http proxy error: /documents/upload (socket hang up / ECONNRESET)
docs.text:
Cause: Occurs if the FastAPI server restarts mid-upload or if the backend process is killed while processing a file.

Fix: app/api.py stores temporary upload files in the OS system temp directory (/tmp/adk_rag_uploads) outside the Uvicorn --reload watch tree and executes ingest_document in a background worker thread (asyncio.to_thread). Ensure you do not edit .py files in the project root while an upload is actively in progress.

docs.title: HTTP 401: Invalid or expired authentication token
docs.text:
Cause: Your JWT session token expired or JWT_SECRET_KEY was changed on the server.

Fix: Click Sign Out in the top-right header bar (or sign in again on the Sign In screen) to obtain a fresh JWT token.

docs.title: HTTP 400: Unsupported file type
docs.text:
Cause: The uploaded file extension is not in the supported list (for example, legacy .doc instead of .docx).

Fix: Convert the file to one of the supported extensions: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .log.

docs.title: ValueError: No readable text was found in the document
docs.text:
Cause: The uploaded PDF contains scanned images without an embedded text layer, or the file is empty.

Fix: Run OCR on scanned PDFs before uploading, or verify the document contains selectable text.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an Account or Sign In
docs.text: When you open the application (http://localhost:5173), the Bioluminescent Neural Forest Authentication Modal appears in front of the Tree of Knowledge backdrop. Every account is stored in the Neon PostgreSQL users table and issues an HS256 signed JWT Bearer token.

docs.title: Sign In to an Existing Workspace
docs.text:
1. Select the Sign In tab on the authentication modal.
  2. Enter your registered Email Address (e.g., dronanaik1133@gmail.com) and Password.
  3. Click Sign In to Workspace → to authenticate against POST /auth/login and enter your isolated workspace.

docs.title: Create a New Account
docs.text:
1. Select the Create Account tab on the authentication card.
  2. Fill in your registration details:
  3. Full Name: Your display name shown in the top workspace header.
  4. Email Address: Your unique workspace identifier (user_id).
  5. Password: Minimum 6 characters, hashed using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 before storage in Neon PostgreSQL.
  6. Click Create Account & Continue → to register via POST /auth/signup and automatically sign in.

Strict Multi-Tenant Data Isolation

Every document you upload, every 768-dimensional vector chunk stored in Neon PostgreSQL, and every :Entity / :RELATES_TO record created in Neo4j is strictly scoped to your authenticated user_id. No other user can view or query your workspace data.

docs.title: Step 1b: Configure Environment Variables (Settings in Top Header)
docs.text:
Immediately after signing in, you land on Settings (SettingsTab.jsx), which lives in the top header bar alongside Evaluation—keeping the main navigation bar focused on the 5 core workflow tabs (Upload → Ingestion Pipeline → Documents → Agentic Chat → Knowledge Graph).

  1. Minimalist Variable Grid: Each card displays only the environment variable key name (GOOGLE_API_KEY, AGENT_MODEL, GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL, EMBEDDING_MODEL, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET_KEY, JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS, NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD, NEO4J_DATABASE, TOP_K), an input field, and an info icon (ⓘ).
  2. Documentation Deep-Link (ⓘ): Clicking the ⓘ icon next to any variable opens the exact step-by-step guide in Installation & Environment Setup explaining how to obtain that key.
  3. Silent Default Fallback: Default values are never exposed in the UI. Leaving any input blank automatically falls back to the server's default configuration in the background.
  4. Click Save & Continue to apply your configuration and automatically navigate to the Upload tab.

docs.title: Step 2: Uploading One or Multiple Documents (Upload Tab)
docs.text: Once your settings are saved, you transition to the Upload tab (UploadTab.jsx).

docs.title: Upload Documents Dropzone
docs.text:
1. Drag and drop one or multiple files onto the dashed bioluminescent dropzone, or click click to browse multiple files to open your system file picker.
  2. All 13 supported file extensions are displayed as badges below the dropzone: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .htm, and .log.

docs.title: Multi-Document Queue Selected & Ready to Ingest
docs.text:
1. Once one or more files are selected (e.g., doc1_openai_funding.md, doc2_anthropic_amazon.md, and doc6_google_ai_strategy.md), the dropzone transforms into an interactive Multi-Document Queue Card displaying:
  2. Selected Count & Total Size Badge: e.g., 3 Documents Selected (Total: 10.9 KB).
  3. Queue Controls: Click + Add More Files to append additional documents to the batch, or Clear All to reset the queue.
  4. Numbered File Preview Rows: Each queued document shows its batch order (1, 2, 3…), format-specific icon, exact filename, formatted file size, and an individual × Remove button.
  5. Click the primary gradient button Ingest 3 Documents into Neon Postgres & Neo4j (or Ingest into Neon Postgres & Neo4j for a single file) at the bottom of the view to launch the 5-step hybrid ingestion pipeline.

docs.title: Step 3: Monitoring the Live 5-Step Ingestion Pipeline (Ingestion Pipeline Tab)
docs.text: Clicking the Ingest button automatically transitions you to the Ingestion Pipeline tab (IngestionTab.jsx), which processes each queued document sequentially through all 5 stages while polling GET /ingest/progress every 450ms.

docs.title: Live Per-Document 5-Step Hybrid Ingestion Execution
docs.text:
While documents are actively being processed:

  • Per-Document Live Progress Banner:
  • When multiple documents are selected, the header badge displays SELECTED DOCUMENT 2 OF 3 • STEP S OF 5 • <STEP NAME> along with a Doc 2 / 3 indicator and the per-document percentage progress bar (0% → 100% for each file).
  • For a single document, it displays STEP S OF 5 • <STEP NAME>.
  • Database Status Cards: Real-time counters for Neon Postgres Status (Ready), Vector Chunks Stored, Neo4j Entities, and Neo4j Relationships update as each document finishes.
  • Active vs. Queued Step Badges:
  • The currently executing stage highlights with a glowing cyan border and a Running Now... spinner badge.
  • Upcoming stages remain in the Queued state until the active stage completes.

docs.title: Completed Batch Ingestion Summary & Stage Logs
docs.text:
When all queued documents finish executing all 5 stages:

  1. Emerald Completion Banner (All 5 Pipeline Steps Completed Successfully (3 Documents Ingested)):
  2. Explicitly displays the total number of ingested documents when a multi-file batch completes.
  3. Summarizes aggregated metrics across the batch (Documents Ingested: 3, Filenames, Chunks (pgvector): 13, Entities (Neo4j): 126, Relationships (Neo4j): 118, and Characters: 11,205).
  4. Lists a Per-Document Breakdown (✓ 1. doc1_openai_funding.md, ✓ 2. doc2_anthropic_amazon.md, ✓ 3. doc6_google_ai_strategy.md) with each file's individual chunk, entity, and relationship counts.
  5. Updated Database Counters: The 4 workspace metric cards immediately reflect the updated totals in Neon PostgreSQL and Neo4j.
  6. Per-Stage Output Logs: All 5 pipeline cards show green ✓ Completed badges along with their concrete stage output for the completed run.

Automatic Redundant & Updated File Upload Handling (v2.1.1)

The ingestion pipeline computes a normalized SHA-256 content fingerprint (content_hash) for every uploaded file and automatically handles redundant or updated uploads:

  • Exact Same File Uploaded Again (Skipped (Already Indexed)): Skips redundant Gemini embedding and Neo4j extraction calls and reuses your existing indexed document.
  • Same Content with a Different Filename (Skipped (Duplicate of <filename>)): Prevents duplicate chunks from skewing vector similarity scores and points to the existing filename.
  • Updated Version of an Existing File (Updated Version): Atomically purges the old version's chunks from Neon PostgreSQL and its relationships/orphaned entities from Neo4j before indexing the updated document.

docs.title: Step 4: Managing Indexed Documents (Documents Tab)
docs.text: Switch to the Documents tab (DocumentsTab.jsx) to audit your indexed files or remove documents from your workspace.

docs.title: Indexed Documents List
docs.text:
Each indexed document card displays:

  • Filename & Format Icon: e.g., doc6_google_ai_strategy.md, doc2_anthropic_amazon.md, and doc1_openai_funding.md
  • Neon PostgreSQL Vector Count Badge: e.g., 7 chunks, 3 chunks (cyan badge)
  • Neo4j Entity Count Badge: e.g., 55 entities, 31 entities, 33 entities (gold badge)
  • Neo4j Relationship Count Badge: e.g., 52 relations, 31 relations, 33 relations (emerald badge)
  • Document UUID: Truncated doc_id (ID: 3cff2396-097...)
  • Refresh & Delete Controls: Top-right Refresh button and per-document Delete button.

docs.title: Atomic Cascade Delete & Bulk "Delete All" Confirmation Modal (v2.3.3)
docs.text:
1. Single-Document Delete: Clicking Delete on any document card reveals an inline confirmation bar: Delete from Postgres & Neo4j? with Yes, delete and Cancel buttons. Clicking Yes, delete invokes DELETE /documents/{doc_id} to atomically remove the document's chunks from Neon PostgreSQL and its relationships/orphaned entities from Neo4j.
  1. Bulk "Delete All" with Type-to-Confirm Popup (Delete):
  2. Clicking the Delete All button in the top-right header opens a modal dialog (Delete All Documents).
  3. To prevent accidental data loss, the Delete All action button remains disabled until you type Delete into the confirmation input field.
  4. Confirming invokes DELETE /documents, wiping all documents, vector chunks, and Knowledge Graph entities/relationships for your user account across both Neon PostgreSQL and Neo4j.

docs.title: Step 5: Asking Questions in Agentic Chat (Agentic Chat Tab)
docs.text: Switch to the Agentic Chat tab (ChatTab.jsx) to converse with the Google ADK LlmAgent powered by Gemini 2.5 Pro.

docs.title: Starter Prompts & New Session View
docs.text:
When starting a new session:

  • Four clickable Starter Question Pills let you immediately test hybrid vector + graph retrieval:
  • "Summarize the key concepts and how they relate to each other."
  • "What are the main entities and relationships in my knowledge graph?"
  • "Explain the core architecture and technical components described."
  • "What are the key findings, metrics, or conclusions?"
  • You can also type any custom question into the bottom input box and press Enter (or click the icon-only Send button).

docs.title: Multi-Tool Grounded Response with Dual Citations
docs.text:
When you submit a cross-document question (e.g., "How do OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon, and Google compare in their AI funding and strategic partnerships?"):

  1. Session Management Controls: The header displays a glowing Session active badge (preserving multi-turn ADK InMemorySessionService memory) and a New session button to reset the conversation.
  2. Tool Execution Badges: At the top of the assistant bubble, tool chips show the exact backend tools the ADK agent autonomously executed (hybrid_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships, or vector_search).
  3. Inline Dual Citations:
  4. Document Chunk Citations ([Source: doc2_anthropic_amazon.md, chunk 1]) highlight in cyan/emerald, linking claims directly to semantic vector chunks in Neon PostgreSQL.
  5. Knowledge Graph Citations ([Graph: Latest Funding Round -> HAS_AMOUNT -> $6.6 Billion]) highlight in gold, tracing multi-hop entity relationships in Neo4j.

docs.title: Step 6: Exploring the Neo4j Knowledge Graph (Knowledge Graph Tab)
docs.text: Switch to the Knowledge Graph tab (GraphTab.jsx) to visually explore and query the domain-agnostic entities and directed relationships extracted from your documents.

docs.title: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Topology Overview
docs.text:
The Neo4j Knowledge Graph Explorer provides four synchronized views:

  1. Graph Summary Cards: Displays Total Entities (179), Relationships (209), and Entity Categories (23).
  2. Real-Time Search & Dynamic Category Filter Pills:
  3. Type any keyword into the search bar to filter entities, relationship types, or facts in real time.
  4. Click any dynamically inferred category pill (All, Organization, Event, Model, Agreement, Funding Round, Metric, Product, Service, Person, Partnership, Document, Location, Infrastructure, AI Model, Initiative, Concept, Feature, Platform, Technology, Alliance, Year, Strategy, Market) to isolate specific node types and their 1-hop neighbors.
  5. Interactive Entity Topology (Left Panel): Renders a radial SVG neural network where hub entities (such as Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic) sit at the center connected to surrounding domain nodes color-coded by category.
  6. Extracted Relationship Facts (Right Panel): Lists all extracted (Source) -[RELATION]-> (Target) triples along with their natural-language fact sentence and source document attribution (doc1_openai_funding.md, doc2_anthropic_amazon.md, doc6_google_ai_strategy.md).

docs.title: Selected Entity 1-Hop Neighborhood Inspector
docs.text:
Clicking any node on the interactive SVG canvas (or clicking any entity name in the right-hand facts list) activates the 1-Hop Neighborhood Inspector:

  1. Gold Neighborhood Highlighting: All edges directly connected to the selected entity (Google) illuminate in gold (#fbbf24) with relationship labels (HAS_MARKET_SHARE_IN, HAS_LONG_TERM_VISION, HAS_INTEGRATED_CAPABILITY, DEVELOPS, ANALYZES) rendered along the connecting paths, while unconnected nodes dim.
  2. Selected Entity Detail Card (Top-Right): Displays the entity's category badge (ORGANIZATION), canonical name (Google), Gemini-extracted summary description ("Google's approach to the AI competitive landscape reveals a sophisticated multi-front strategy that simultaneously develops internal capabilities while investing in potential competitors."), and a × Clear button to return to the full graph view.
  3. Filtered Entity Relationships List (Bottom-Right): Automatically filters the right-hand panel (Relationships for "Google") to show only the 38 triples involving the selected node.

docs.title: Step 7: Evaluating RAG Quality (Evaluation in Top Header)
docs.text: Click Evaluation in the top header bar (EvaluationTab.jsx) to measure the accuracy, grounding, and routing quality of your Agentic RAG pipeline using Gemini 2.5 Flash as an LLM-as-a-Judge and optional LangSmith experiment tracking.

docs.title: Generate a Synthetic Golden Dataset
docs.text:
1. Choose the number of synthetic Q&A test cases (3, 5, or 8 Questions) in the Golden Dataset card.
  2. Click Generate Golden Dataset (POST /evals/generate-dataset) to sample indexed chunks from your Neon PostgreSQL workspace and synthesize grounded (question, expected_answer, category, source_doc) pairs via Gemini 2.5 Flash.
  3. If LANGSMITH_API_KEY is configured, the dataset is automatically synced to your LangSmith workspace for reproducible experiment tracking.

docs.title: Run Evaluation & Inspect Per-Case Scores
docs.text:
1. Click Run Evaluation (POST /evals/run) to execute every golden question through the live ADK Agent (hybrid_search, graph_search, vector_search, get_entity_relationships) and score each response across 5 metrics:
  2. Faithfulness: Are claims strictly supported by retrieved chunks and graph facts?
  3. Context Relevance: Did the retrieved context target the user's question?
  4. Answer Correctness: Does the generated answer match the expected ground truth?
  5. Tool Routing: Did the ADK agent invoke appropriate search tools?
  6. Citation Compliance: Did the answer include [Source: ...] or [Graph: ...] inline citations?
  7. Inspect the Experiment Results summary KPIs (Overall Score, Cases Evaluated, per-metric averages, and LangSmith run link when enabled) and expand any individual case to compare the Agent Answer, Expected Answer, retrieved tool calls, and judge reasoning.
